explanation: Across the Gulf, the sole of the foot is viewed as the dirtiest part of the body because it touches the ground, so deliberately pointing it at someone is read as a strong insult. This is a regional cultural custom rather than an Islamic legal rule, but it is taken seriously in Emirati homes, majlis seating, and any formal gathering where people sit on low cushions or face each other directly.
local_tip: Keep both feet flat on the floor or tucked beneath you, and avoid resting an ankle on a knee in a way that points your sole at anyone.

also_check.note: The feet are considered the lowest and most impure part of the body, so pointing them at a person or a Buddha image is a serious taboo.
Deliberately showing the soles of your feet, especially on tatami mats or in temples, is seen as careless and disrespectful.
Showing the soles of your feet is generally neutral and only seems informal in unusually formal settings.
